id: title:danielcarletti:correct the repartition wording in django admin

review.posthog_relevance: Updates warehouse user-facing help text and button labels regarding warehouse table repartition and reload behavior, removing references to a deprecated 'reset resync' workflow.
review.reason: The changes are strictly limited to help text and button labels in the warehouse management UI. P1.F1.H1 updates the section title and help text; P1.F1.H2 updates the button label and confirmation message; P1.F1.H3 updates help text regarding ad-hoc sync. No backend implementation, query, or execution logic is changed. This is a documentation and UI clarification change.
review.uncertainty: The tier is assigned based solely on the absence of backend implementation changes. The score does not account for potential downstream effects of the removed 'reset resync' workflow, which are not observable in this diff. The benefit is limited to user comprehension, not system behavior or reliability.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, conservative group. No tier assignment is made; only observations are returned.

observations.behavior: The hunk P1.F1.H1 removes the phrase 'Repartition & resync' and replaces it with 'Repartition', while also removing the help text that described a workflow with reset_pipeline=true and replacing it with new help text describing an incremental or append-only table rewrite and a full refresh table reload. This changes the displayed help and the section title.
observations.code_quote: run. For an incremental or append-only table the run rewrites the files already in
observations.posthog_connection: This changes the help text shown to warehouse users, removing the instruction and warning about a reset and replacing it with an explanation of the rewrite and reload behavior. This could help users understand the behavior of the repartition action without needing to read the backend implementation.

observations.behavior: The hunk P1.F1.H2 changes the button's data-confirm attribute and the button's label. The label changes from 'Repartition & resync' to 'Repartition', and the confirmation message changes from 'Repartition + reset resync' to a message describing the rewrite and reload behavior.
observations.code_quote: data-confirm="Repartition this table (non-billable)? An incremental or append-only table is rewritten in place. A full refresh table, or one with a reset pending, is reloaded from the source.">
observations.posthog_connection: This changes the button label and the confirmation message shown to warehouse users, removing the reference to a reset and replacing it with an explanation of the rewrite and reload behavior. This could help users understand the behavior of the repartition action without needing to read the backend implementation.

observations.behavior: The hunk P1.F1.H3 changes the help text under the 'Trigger ad-hoc sync' section. The phrase 'already triggers its own non-billable reset resync' is replaced with 'already triggers its own non-billable run'. This removes the reference to a reset and replaces it with a reference to a run.
observations.code_quote: already triggers its own non-billable run — don't double up.
observations.posthog_connection: This changes the help text shown to warehouse users, removing the reference to a reset and replacing it with a reference to a run. This could help users understand the behavior of the repartition action without needing to read the backend implementation.
